notes: Material limits on how to read the result (not failures). (a) Our scenarios are saturated for recall@5: median conversation length is 3 turns (125 of 132 gold-bearing dev cases have at most 5 turns, 129 have as_of_seq <= 5), so k=5 returns almost the whole conversation. Dense, hybrid and w3 variants are all 1.0, and only bm25 separates from the rest on that source. The 'winner' is therefore effectively decided on QMSum, and the ours source is weak evidence. MRR on ours is more informative; 16 of 148 ours cases have no gold and are excluded from recall. (b) Recall is any-gold-hit. QMSum gold spans are wide (median 21 turns, max 580, mean about 10 percent of the meeting), which makes recall@5 easier than a single-turn lookup; absolute QMSum numbers should not be read as single-evidence-turn retrieval. (c) Windows are credited by expanding to their member turns and a hit anywhere in a window counts for all 3 turns, which mildly favours w3, yet w3 still loses clearly on QMSum (hybrid_t1 minus dense_w3 +0.167, CI [0.12, 0.216]). A 10-turn ranking holds about 4 windows, so w3 sees fewer distinct locations at k=5. (d) The winner is not measurably different from dense_t1 and hybrid_rerank_t1 on QMSum (CI includes 0) or from dense/hybrid/rerank variants on ours; hybrid_t1 is a rule-based pick, not a demonstrated improvement over those. It does measurably beat bm25 on both sources and every w3 variant on QMSum. (e) Labels unreviewed (labels_reviewed false), so these results are provisional. (f) The record timestamps read 2026-11-03 UTC, while the commit times are 2026-11-02 PT; they are consistent. (g) check_run on a mislabelled record ran about 3 minutes per full bootstrap; the full E1 check takes about 11 minutes.
